payload.headline: READ THE SPEC, NOT THE AGENT PROSE — the consumer has NO nearest-file scan. My prior tolerance-window remedy was designed against behaviour I inferred from one agent sentence and never verified.

spec_verbatim.tick_rule: TICK = current UTC time formatted as HH:MM (round to nearest 5-min slot)
spec_verbatim.lookup: single exact-path existence check; if present, a >7min staleness test on THAT file; else fall through to direct MCP

payload.true_mechanism: FOUR quantizations of one clock, not a sub-minute race: writer names by RAW minute (date -u +%H:%M, tick-snapshot.md); reader looks up the SAME clock ROUNDED TO 5-MIN SLOTS; promotion looks up the NOMINAL QUARTER TICK. A write can only ever be found when its minute is a multiple of 5.

corrections_to_my_own_prior_claims.claim: the 03:00Z HIT was luck — a write at 03:05:45Z reached inside the remaining 15 seconds
corrections_to_my_own_prior_claims.why: minute 05 is a multiple of 5, so the rounded lookup resolves 03:05 for any read from 03:02:30 to 03:07:30. That HIT was DETERMINISTIC with a ~5-minute window, not a 15-second coin flip.

corrections_to_my_own_prior_claims.claim: the consumer locates the neighbouring file and computes its staleness, then discards it on name equality alone
corrections_to_my_own_prior_claims.why: built on the 03:30Z agent sentence about a nearest file being 1 min stale. The spec has no nearest-neighbour scan. That was agent narration read as code behaviour.

corrections_to_my_own_prior_claims.claim: cheaper remedy = a tolerance window on the nearest snapshot the consumer already computes
corrections_to_my_own_prior_claims.why: there is no nearest-snapshot computation to put a tolerance on. That remedy would have to BUILD the scan first, so it is not the cheap option it was sold as.

corrections_to_my_own_prior_claims.claim: margin_to_minute_roll_seconds is the discriminator (recorded in the 03:45Z telemetry signal)
corrections_to_my_own_prior_claims.why: the reader rounds to 5-min buckets, so distance to the next MINUTE is not the relevant quantity; distance to the next 5-MIN BUCKET boundary is.

what_still_holds: The prediction was right: 03:45Z tick MISSED, as called in advance in commit 09a5c4297. 4 samples, 2 advance predictions, both held.
Promotion is structurally unsatisfiable: 0 of 46 files carry a nominal-quarter name.
cycle-snapshot-latest.json frozen at tick 00:00 / 2026-08-23T00:07:50Z, serving regime UNKNOWN vs live NEUTRAL.
Blast radius still bounded: every miss falls back to live MCP calls, so the cost is ~2 redundant bootstrap calls per tick, not wrong data.
remedy_now_single: Name by NOMINAL tick in all three places (writer, reader, promotion). The dispatcher already passes scheduled_utc, so the writer has the nominal value in hand and does not need to derive it. This is the only remedy that fixes reader AND promotion; there is no cheap second option.
unresolved: At 03:45Z the agent reported the latest cached snapshot was from the prior day, while at 03:30Z the same agent on the same flow reported a nearest file 1 min stale. The spec explains neither phrasing. Treat both as narration of unknown provenance, not as evidence of lookup behaviour.
